chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ala'a ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man washes and he intends to enter the state of Ihram, so he wears a shirt before he recites the Talbiyya, then upon him is (repeating of) the washing.

key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: enters the state of Ihram (sacred consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one puts on Ihram clothes before reciting the Talbiyya after bathing?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the precise sequence of actions required for the validity of the ritual bath (Ghusl) for Ihram, emphasizing that the state of ritual purity is contingent upon the immediate intention and action of donning garments before the verbal declaration. In Shia fiqh, this underscores the importance of maintaining the continuity of the Ghusl's effects until the specific act of entering the sacred state is completed, ensuring the pilgrim remains in a state of purity throughout the transition.
